title: Big Buck Hunter
headline: One shotgun, four hunters, and a doe you must not shoot.
intro: Big Buck Hunter: Call of the Wild puts one pump-action shotgun in front of a hunting-lodge scene and up to four credit-paying hunters taking turns with it — not a simultaneous two-player shootout. Insert credit, pick a region on a relief map, then separate antlered bucks from does in a running herd before the window closes. Every trigger pull flashes the whole screen white so the gun's optics can read the shot; the pump racks a fresh shell between pulls. Shoot a doe and the hunt ends immediately — the entire game's tension sits in that one rule.

referenceScope.primary: Big Buck Hunter: Call of the Wild (2006)
referenceScope.reason: Chosen within the Big Buck Hunter family for the richest verifiable source set found — a full operator manual, a real cabinet photo, and version-matched screenshots, not because a build was pre-selected.
referenceScope.caveat: Earlier single-gun titles in this family differ in content, and Big Buck Hunter Pro onward (2006, Raw Thrills) is a two-gun generation (see Release Notes). No cabinet or software version has been chosen, and no game has been run, emulated, or measured here.

session.format: Up to four hunters take turns with one shared shotgun and one credit-metered game — not simultaneous two-player play.
session.social: Players hand the gun off between turns; the group watches the current hunter and calls out buck-or-doe decisions from the sideline.
session.failureToAvoid: Adding a second gun holster or implying co-op play: the manual's wiring references only 'GUN 1', and Wikipedia confirms the pre-2006 series was single-gun, round-robin for up to four players.

playLoop.title: Buy In
playLoop.action: Insert credit and pick a cost tier — a single Trip, a full Region pass, Hunt Club, Bonus Only, or Tournament on an ITNet-registered cabinet.
playLoop.feedback: The coin-door Player Cost Schedule prices each tier separately.
playLoop.skill: Decide how much game you want before the clock starts.

playLoop.title: Pick a Region
playLoop.action: Aim the shotgun's reticle at a wedge of the US/Canada relief map and pull the trigger to select, under a visible countdown.
playLoop.feedback: The chosen region and day count load onscreen.
playLoop.skill: Reading the map fast doubles as a first test of the gun's aim.

playLoop.title: Pick a Stand
playLoop.action: Choose one of several buck-photo stands laid over a state map, e.g. 'IOWA — DAY 1 of 5'.
playLoop.feedback: Score resets to zero and a short countdown starts as the scene loads.
playLoop.skill: Different stands bias which terrain and animals appear next.

playLoop.title: Hunt
playLoop.action: Raise the shotgun, track moving deer or elk, and fire only once antlers are visible on a legal buck; pump the slide between shots.
playLoop.feedback: A trigger pull flashes the screen white so the gun's optics can read the aim point; a hit buck drops, a hit doe ends the hunt.
playLoop.skill: Snap identification — separating antlers from no-antlers in a running herd before the window closes.

playLoop.title: Bonus Round
playLoop.action: Between treks, a bonus stage (Skeet, Duck, Raccoon Rampage, Wild Boar, and others) swaps the hunting scene for a faster target gallery.
playLoop.feedback: The same gun is used, but scoring and pace differ and the doe penalty does not apply.
playLoop.skill: A change of pace that still rewards fast, accurate shooting.

screenRead.label: MONEY IN counter
screenRead.meaning: Running total of credits inserted this game, shown during attract mode and live play.

screenRead.label: Antlers vs. no antlers
screenRead.meaning: The only visual cue separating a legal buck from a doe that ends the hunt if hit — there is no other HUD marker.

screenRead.label: Reticle
screenRead.meaning: Shows where the optical gun is aimed; the same cursor navigates the region and stand-select menus.

screenRead.label: Day counter and countdown timer
screenRead.meaning: 'DAY 1 of 5' tracks trek progress; a small numeric timer counts down the seconds left to tag the day's target.

gameplayStoryboard.summary: Five-stage walkthrough of one hunting trek, from region/stand select through a bonus-stage detour, built from Call of the Wild's documented optical-shotgun controls (BBH1) and its one confirmed on-screen identification rule — antlers or not (BBH3). Camera direction is proposed presentation for a current-tech rebuild; the single-gun, round-robin turn structure and the doe penalty are carried over exactly as sourced, not reinterpreted.

stages.title: Region and stand select: aim, pull, commit
stages.playerAction: After inserting credit and choosing a cost tier, the player aims the shotgun's reticle at a wedge of the US/Canada relief map and pulls the trigger to pick a region, then selects a buck-photo stand on the state map the same way, under a visible countdown.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: wide lodge-map camera centered on the relief map, with the reticle as the only visible cursor and the countdown timer framed in a corner.
onScreen: Reticle cursor reused for menu selection (documented control re-use, BBH1)
stages.feedback: Selecting a region or stand loads its day count, e.g. 'DAY 1 of 5', resets score to zero, and loads the hunting scene.
stages.decision: Player picks which region and stand biases the terrain and animals that appear in the hunt to come.

stages.title: Raise the shotgun, track the herd
stages.playerAction: Player raises the mounted shotgun and tracks moving deer or elk crossing the scene, watching for antlers before committing a shot.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: hunting-blind POV at shoulder height, wide enough to hold the running herd in frame as it crosses.
onScreen: Antlers vs. no antlers — the only visual cue separating a legal buck from a doe (documented HUD, BBH3)
Reticle tracking the shotgun's current aim point (documented control, BBH1)
Countdown timer ticking down the window to tag the target (documented HUD, BBH7)
stages.feedback: Each animal's antler state is the only information offered before the shot — there is no other on-screen marker.
stages.decision: Player decides which animal in the running herd, if any, is a legal buck worth the single shot.

stages.title: Fire: the screen-flash shot resolves the hit
stages.playerAction: Player pulls the trigger on a legal-looking buck. The gun's optics read the exact aim point at the instant of the flash.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: hold on the aim point through the flash, then cut to the result — buck drop or doe penalty — without breaking continuity from the tracking frame.
onScreen: Full-screen white flash timed to the trigger pull (documented mechanic, BBH1)
Hit resolution: a tagged buck drops; a hit doe ends the hunt immediately (documented rule, BBH3)
stages.feedback: A correct buck shot banks the tag toward the day count; a doe hit ends the hunt on the spot — the single rule the whole hunt hinges on.
stages.decision: The identification made while tracking is now graded instantly by the flash-timed hit read, with no appeal.

stages.title: Pump, re-acquire, keep hunting
stages.playerAction: Player racks the pump slide to chamber the next shot, then re-raises and re-tracks the herd for the next legal buck before the day's countdown expires.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: quick insert on the pump's sliding throw, then back to the wide tracking frame.
onScreen: Day counter and countdown timer continuing from region/stand select (documented HUD, BBH7)
Herd continuing to move across the scene, consistent with the documented running-herd hunt format (BBH1)
stages.feedback: A successful pump readies the next shot without losing the aim point; a fumbled pump costs time against the countdown.
stages.decision: Player decides whether to keep hunting the current stand or let the day's countdown lapse and move on.

stages.title: Bonus stage: same gun, faster gallery
stages.playerAction: Between treks, the game swaps into a bonus stage — Skeet, Duck, Raccoon Rampage, Wild Boar, or others — using the same shotgun, with different scoring, faster pace, and no doe penalty.
stages.camera: Proposed presentation: tighter gallery framing suited to fast-moving bonus targets rather than the wide hunting-scene frame.
onScreen: Bonus-stage scoring distinct from the hunting score (documented mode difference, BBH2/BBH6)
No antler-identification cue — the doe penalty does not apply here (documented, BBH2/BBH6)
stages.feedback: Fast, accurate shooting is rewarded on its own terms, without the hunt's identification tension.
stages.decision: Player adapts aim/trigger timing to a faster, differently scored gallery instead of the hunt's identify-then-shoot rhythm.

signatureMoments.title: The screen-flash shot
signatureMoments.description: Every trigger pull blinks the whole monitor solid white for an instant. Not a visual flourish — the manufacturer's own gun-and-monitor diagnostic test documents this as how the gun's optical sensor measures exactly where the barrel pointed at the moment of the shot.

signatureMoments.title: The doe that ends it
signatureMoments.description: Wikipedia's own gameplay summary states plainly: shoot a female animal and the player is out. With bucks and does mixed in a running herd, that single rule turns every shot into a split-second identification call.

signatureMoments.title: Regional bonus detours
signatureMoments.description: Raccoon Rampage and Wild Boar Bonus were the headline new modes in the 2006 update's own sales flyer — a deliberate break from the hunting loop into faster, differently scored target galleries.

controls.action: Fires a shot at the current aim point; on menus it scrolls down / confirms.
controls.feel: The one input every hit or miss comes down to — a build must keep optical-flash timing tight enough that the read never lags the real pull.

controls.action: Racks the shotgun between shots; on menus it scrolls up.
controls.feel: A real, spring-loaded gesture — the manual documents pump and trigger as separate switches, not a single trigger-only input, so a panel must preserve a sliding throw, not a second button.

controls.action: Points the reticle; the gun reads its position via the flash-sync technique above.
controls.feel: Must tolerate the same bright-light and glare sensitivity the manual's own troubleshooting section names as a known failure mode.

controls.action: Confirms a highlighted menu choice alongside the gun's trigger/pump scrolling.
controls.feel: Shares its vocabulary with the shotgun controls — no redundant separate confirm button is needed.

buildPriorities.title: One gun, not two
buildPriorities.why: The Eagle-era kit wires exactly one gun ('GUN 1' is the only connector referenced in the 47-page manual and in the MAME driver's own input list, and the original kit ships a single Gun Assembly); Wikipedia confirms the pre-2006 series was 'a single gun platform' with players rotating turns.
buildPriorities.proof: A finished bench accepts four separate coin-ins and runs four full turns with only one gun wired.

buildPriorities.title: Preserve the screen-flash shot timing
buildPriorities.why: Hit detection is a real-time optical read keyed to a full-screen flash on every trigger pull; added display latency or a panel that can't reproduce that flash breaks the actual aiming feedback loop, not just the visuals.
buildPriorities.proof: A bench trigger pull shows the flash and the hit/miss register with the same felt timing as reference footage.

buildPriorities.title: Keep the pump a real sliding throw
buildPriorities.why: The manual spring-loads pump and trigger as separate switches and names 'Traditional Pump-Action Shotgun' a feature across releases; a second button would remove the one tactile detail that sells the shotgun fantasy.
buildPriorities.proof: A player can tell trigger from pump by feel alone with eyes closed.

buildPriorities.title: Make the doe penalty immediate and legible
buildPriorities.why: The hunting loop's entire risk rests on one instant call — antlers or not — with a hard, on-the-spot penalty for guessing wrong; ambiguous or delayed hit feedback erases that tension.
buildPriorities.proof: A first-time player can state, unprompted, why their hunt just ended after shooting a doe.

releaseNotes.title: Call of the Wild (2006) vs. the original 2000 Big Buck Hunter
releaseNotes.body: Both are the same single-gun Eagle-era hardware family (MAME driver ids bbh, bbhsc, bbh2sp, bbhcotw), but the 2006 update adds the Midwest and Southwest regions, elk and antelope, an expanded Hunt Club mode, and the Raccoon Rampage / Wild Boar bonus rounds — none on the original 2000 cabinet's software.

releaseNotes.title: Violence settings are an operator choice, not a player one
releaseNotes.body: The manual documents three selectable modes — Normal (visible blood), No Blood (bloodless, audio-only), and Tagging Only (no kill references) — set once by the operator in Test Mode, not chosen per player.

releaseNotes.title: Pro, Safari, HD, and Reloaded are a different, two-gun generation
releaseNotes.body: Beginning with Big Buck Hunter Pro (2006, Raw Thrills), the series moved to a two-gun cabinet with genuine head-to-head competition — a different control contract from this release's single gun, not a drop-in upgrade.
